neighbours.label: learning by example: the verb slot where someone does what they saw a model do (imitation, 'if she can do it, so can you')
fire: Toddlers who see their older sisters brushing their teeth soon want to brush their own.
My dad fixed his own car, so I figured I could learn to do the same.
Boys who watch their fathers shout at referees often start shouting too.
Study how the senior nurse talks to patients and try to speak the way she does.
If your neighbour managed to grow tomatoes on a balcony, you can do it as well.
Students tend to copy the habits of the teachers they admire most.
Seeing her mentor run a marathon at sixty made her believe she could run one too.
Puppies learn to sit faster when they watch an older dog obey the command.
quiet: Toddlers who brush their teeth twice a day get fewer cavities later on.
My dad sold his old car last spring and bought a bicycle instead.
Boys who play football after school often sleep better at night.
The senior nurse talks to every patient before the morning rounds begin.
Tomatoes grown on a sunny balcony need watering at least once a day.
Students tend to remember lessons better when they get enough sleep.
Her mentor ran a marathon at sixty and finished in under five hours.
Puppies need several small meals a day until they are six months old.

notes: Top examples are advice about copying others; the output suppresses replicate/copy/mimic. Probe: imitation sentences 0.2-0.33, neutral controls under 0.01.
